Let <MATH_0001>.
Let <MATH_0002> be a scheme contained in a big site <MATH_0003>.
Let <MATH_0004> be a <MATH_0005>-sheaf
satisfying property (b) of Lemma <REF_0001> with
<MATH_0006>. Then the extension
<MATH_0007> of <MATH_0008> to the category of all schemes over <MATH_0009>
satisfies the sheaf condition for all <MATH_0010>-coverings.

This follows from Lemma <REF_0001>
applied with <MATH_0001>.
Conditions (1), (2), (a), and (b) of Lemma <REF_0002>
hold; we omit the details. Thus we get our unique extension <MATH_0002>
to the category of all schemes over <MATH_0003>. Finally, observe that
any standard <MATH_0004>-covering is tautologically equivalent to a
covering in <MATH_0005>, see Sets, Lemma <REF_0003>
as well as Lemmas <REF_0004>,
<REF_0005>,
<REF_0006>,
<REF_0007>, and
<REF_0008>. By
Sites, Lemma <REF_0009>
the sheaf property passes through tautological equivalence
of coverings. Hence the fact that <MATH_0006> is a <MATH_0007>-sheaf implies
that property (c) of Lemma <REF_0010> holds
and we conclude.
